newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Paper says considering merger with Jujo.
newsitem.headline: Japan Paper says considering merger with Jujo.

text.p: Japan's leading paperboard maker, Japan Paper Industry Co Ltd, announced on Friday that it is considering a merger with another paperboard maker, Jujo Paper Board Co Ltd.
The announcement followed an earlier media report that Japan Paper and Jujo Paper Board, both in the Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd group, would merge in October.
The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Friday that a merged firm would make it the country's second-largest paperboard producer after Oji Paper Co Ltd.

Japan Paper said that it was considering a merger with Jujo Paper on condition that the company would be able to remain listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange after the merger and win the necessary approval from the government.
"At the moment, no decision has yet been made," the company said in a statement, adding that it could not comment further.

The company also denied the newspaper's report that it plans to take over the paperboard marketing operations of Nippon Paper subsidiary Tohoku Paper Industries Co Ltd, a paperboard company in northern Japan.
"What was reported on Tohoku Paper is not under consideration," the company said in the statement.
Earlier on Friday morning, the Tokyo Stock Exchange suspended trade in Japan Paper shares for a full day because of a lack of clarity stemming from the media reports.
The newspaper reported that total annual sales of the merged firm are expected to top 100 billion yen, while paperboard output is seen rising to around 1.5 million tonnes per year.

The likely merger is taken as part of Nippon Paper's efforts to streamline its paperboard business, the newspaper said, adding that it might lead to an overall restructuring of the paperboard industry, analysts said.
